en: The Sequential Ritual for Making Offerings to King Yama,
composed by the Tripitaka Master Amogha.
If a practitioner wishes to cultivate this rite, they must first understand the five transformations of this king’s body.
Furthermore, regarding each of the great palaces and their respective dependent originations,
there are five transformations.
The first is Yama, the Dharma King.
These are his original names:
first, the King of Death;
second, the King of the Yellow Springs; and third, King Shanhe Luo.
The fourth is the Wrathful King Vighnāntaka;
the fifth is the Wrathful King Takkirāja.
Their original palaces are located within the lands to the north of the Cakravāḍa Mountains.
This is the palace of the Netherworld (Yama).
It is surrounded by a retinue of fifty thousand.
In the courtyard of the palace stands a *tandana* banner.
Upon its head was a small face of slight wrath;
the King would constantly observe this face to discern the lightness or gravity, and the good or evil, of human offenses.
Whenever there were those among humans who committed grave crimes, [the face would manifest].
From his mouth, flames of fire issue forth, and from within those flames, black ropes surge out to provide warning.
Seeing the wooden splinters, he knows their names and records them.
Furthermore, there are those who perform virtuous deeds.
A white lotus flower blossomed from his mouth,
its fragrance universally perfuming the Great Mountain Lord and the King of the Five Paths General.
Constantly upholding the King’s teachings, he is able to determine good and evil.
Whenever one wishes to practice this Dharma, one should prepare offerings.
Kings, princes, high officials, ministers, and the common people—
each person should provide offerings according to their capacity.
Sesame oil, five-grain paper-money, silk, incense, medicinal herbs, and so forth are used [as offerings].
Butter, honey, *agaru* (aloe) incense, medicinal herbs,
and so forth may be mixed into gruel and boiled.
Seek out a secluded and quiet place in the open air;
it is fitting to cultivate offerings there, lest those who do not understand see them.
Use willow branches five feet long to mark their positions according to this instruction.
At times when this Dharma is afflicted by pestilence, miasmic diseases, and all manner of suffering and distress,
one should cultivate it and practice it concurrently; thus,
one’s karmic retribution will be exhausted and one will be removed from the registers of death.
One should be able to petition the King to erase one's name from the register of death and entrust it to the register of life.
Upon arriving at the house of one afflicted by pestilence,
one should recite the Dàshān Fǔjūn zhòu (Dharani of the Great Mountain Lord) many times.
The practitioner takes their seat, applies fragrant paste, and rubs their arms.
They should recite the name of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni seven times, saying "Namo Śākyamuni Tathāgata.
Then, they sprinkle scented water upon the ground and consecrate bamboo leaves with the scented water.
The mantra is:

Oṃ amṛte hana hana hūṃ svāhā. Because the master of the offering, in a single moment of mental application, is free from the distinction between self and other, it is called the "unrestricted mind" (asaṃvara-citta).
To sever the notions of enemy and kin is called equanimity.
To be able to practice this dharma is the bodhisattva’s vast vow;
it is that which can transport one through compassion.
This is the Tathāgata’s compassion;
it is the king of all merits and stands above the three types of giving.
This is truly due to the power of the empowerment of the Buddha’s supreme, wondrous mantra of inexhaustible majesty, sovereign power, and radiant light,
which can cause a single meal to become an immeasurable amount of food.
Furthermore, one causes each single possession to become inexhaustible wealth;
each and every portion of food, equal in measure to the Dharma-realm,
is universally bestowed upon sentient beings.
All were fully satisfied with the ambrosial food of the Dharma;
their bodies satiated by this Dharma-food, their transgressions were extinguished and merit was generated.
They abandoned the bodies of the evil realms and received the retributions of humans and devas.
It enables the donor to increase their lifespan and eliminate karmic obstacles;
they shall immediately fulfill the dāna-pāramitā, manifestly attract superior fruits, and realize bodhi in the future.
With inconceivable and wondrous power, one believes without delusion.
Today, a certain donor, on behalf of the Emperor, the ministers, and all sentient beings of the Dharma realm,
has universally established this vast and unobstructed offering.
First, record their names and registers, starting from the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Vajra-devas,
down to the various classes of spirits, the paths of the underworld, the hungry ghosts,
monks, nuns, and the deceased.
Establish each one upon the altar,
place the ritual offerings before the register,
and recite the Amṛtakuṇḍalī mantra.
Visualize the empowerment of the offering substances:
within the palm of the right hand is a syllable,
from which flows nectar-water.

Having filled [the vessels] with various offerings and so forth, sprinkle the purified water while reciting the mantra: *Oṃ vajraśāni hūṃ phaṭ*. Sprinkle the aforementioned scented water using a bamboo twig.
If you practice this dharma in an open space,
do not face the roots of peach or willow trees.
Next, you should invite all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
With single-minded devotion, I invoke our Original Teacher, Śākyamuni Buddha.
With single-minded devotion, I invoke the world-protecting deities of vast majesty and sovereign power.
With single-minded devotion, I invoke Amitābha Buddha of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss.
With single-minded devotion, I entreat the Honored Buddha Maitreya, who shall descend to be born in the future;
with single-minded devotion, I entreat all Buddhas throughout the entirety of space;
with single-minded devotion, I entreat the Great Holy Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva.
With single-minded devotion, I entreat the Great Holy Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra.
With single-minded devotion, I entreat the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara of Great Compassion.
With single-minded devotion, I entreat the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta.
With single-minded devotion, I entreat the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas Bhaiṣajyarāja and Bhaiṣajyasamudgata;
with single-minded devotion, I entreat the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin;
with single-minded devotion, I entreat the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha.
With single-minded devotion, I entreat the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha.
With single-minded devotion, I entreat the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajragarbha.
With single-minded devotion, I entreat all the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas throughout the entirety of the realm of space in the ten directions.
With single-minded devotion, I invite all the śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and all worthy sages throughout the ten directions and the entirety of space.
With single-minded devotion, I invite all the dharmapālas, vajrapāṇis, guhyapatis, and the assembly of all benevolent deities.
I only pray that our Original Teacher, Śākyamuni Tathāgata,
as well as all the Buddhas and Great Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas throughout the ten directions, filling all of space and pervading the entire Dharma-realm.
Today, at this very moment, all you hosts of worthy and holy ones have not forsaken your great vows;
for the sake of sentient beings, you have accepted our invitation and descended to this site of practice.
I accept this offering presented by the patron [Name] here and now.
I shall now, relying upon the mantra of invocation, summon the spirits of the netherworld.
I pray that the Triple Gem will compassionately accept this, protect [Name], and eliminate all calamities and misfortunes.
If this person’s retribution for their primary karma is exhausted and they have been entered into the register of death,
may the King, out of compassion and through skillful means, strike out their name from the register of death;
by virtue of his great vow, we pray that he instead place them in the register of life.
"May one live for a hundred years and witness a hundred autumns," and so forth.
Then, he recited the mantra for summoning and gathering all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas:
*Namaḥ samantabuddhānām āḥ sarvatrāpratihatadharmatājñānaprabhūtakasvāhā*. [The mudrā: Form both hands into the wrathful (*krodha*) binding.
The two winds bend like a hook.
Once you have understood this, offer the ritual substances first to Śākyamuni.

Next, if one employs the methods of the royal law, one should first invite the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas and offer them worship in succession; thereafter, one may invite Brahmā, Śakra, and the Four Heavenly Kings. Joining the palms in the seal of the Vajra, one should recite their names. Each of the seats of the Four Heavenly Kings has a spirit; that of the east is named Gandharva King.
In the south is King Kumbhāṇḍa;
in the west are the various nāgas;
and in the north are the twenty-eight great yakṣas.
Having completed the offerings, next [perform] the mudrās and mantras of Mahābrahmā, Śakra, and the Four Great Kings.
For the heart-mantra of the Four Great Kings, the mudrā involves the left hand’s thumb.
The middle fingers and little fingers are both extended upward;
the index fingers and ring fingers are bent,
with the fists resting upon the palms.
With the palms facing forward,
bend the elbows upward.
The mantra says:
Oṃ 1. Jambhara 2. Khānadhara 3. Svāhā 4. For the Brahmā mudrā: form a fist with the left hand and place it on the waist;
extend the five fingers of the right hand upward.
Place it slightly bent so that its height exceeds the shoulders.
Observe that there is a lotus flower within the palms.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ mṛhāṇi svāhā. Next is the seal of Śakra-devendra:
the right hand is placed at the waist as before;
the five fingers of the left hand are extended straight upward.
The two fingers [of the thumbs] touch the earth element;
bend the middle joints so that the wind element touches the back of the fire element;
and bend the middle joints of the space element.
The mantra is:
Oṃ indraya svāhā. For the summoning mudrā of Yama-danda, interlace the middle, ring, and little fingers of both hands.
The two index fingers are raised with their tips touching;
the two thumbs each rest against the side of an index finger;
the palms are opened like the gesture for cupping water.
Move the thumb back and forth.
The mantra is:
*Tadyathā* (1) *oṃ* (2) *yamadaṇḍaya* (3) *śibhaṅkarī* (4) *vajridutite* (5) *hūṃ hūṃ* (6) *svāhā* (7). This is the Dharma-body mudrā of King Yama. Bend the three fingers of the left hand.
Still refer to it as being about one-third of the length of the index finger;
with the thumb broad,
it should be attached to the joint-texture of the lower phalanx of the index finger.
Move the index finger back and forth.
The mantra is:
Oṃ yamarāja ugra-vīrya ajaya svāhā. If one employs this dharma-seal and mantra to construct a great maṇḍala.
To make offerings to all the Buddhas, devas, and others,
one should form this mudrā seven times and recite the mantra;
then King Yama will immediately come to receive these offerings.
With great joy,
next invite the General-King of the Five Paths;
join your palms in the vajra gesture and call his name.
It is said: "The Generals of the Five Paths, the Left Minister of Destiny, and the Right Minister of Destiny.

Next, we invite the Lord of the Heavenly Court, all the officials and subordinate staff of the various heavenly bureaus, the messengers of the Ministry of Public Works, and all other categories of beings."
Descend upon this altar to accept my offerings:

the Lord of the Underworld, the Great King Pyeongdŭng, all the officials and subordinates of the various bureaus of the underworld, the messengers of the Ministry of Personnel, and the various classes of departmental functionaries.
Descend upon this ritual arena and accept my offerings, together with your retinue:
the thirty-six lords of the hells, the horse-headed rākṣasas, the ox-headed rākṣasas, and all others.
Descend upon this ritual arena and accept my offerings.
O Earth-Ruler Vidyārāja, mountains, rivers, peaks, and marshes;
city guardians, local deities, and all assemblies of spirits, each together with your retinues.
I pray that you will come to the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa) to accept my offerings.
As for those among the monastics who have not yet attained liberation,
their patrons may have passed away seven generations ago, long since deceased.
May all spirits and karmic creditors from beginningless time descend to this ritual site to receive my offerings.
May the Great Powerful King of the Burning Face and immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of *gangesālukā* sands of hungry ghosts likewise descend.
May each of you, together with your retinues, descend to this site of practice and accept my offerings.
I take refuge in the Triple Gem.

Next, one invokes the mantra for the hungry ghosts (preta). With the right hand, press the tip of the middle finger with the thumb, and slightly bend the remaining three fingers to produce the sound of a snap.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ bhu-bhū-ri-kāri-ttri-tathāgata-ya. Next, recite the mantra of the throat-opening mudrā; without releasing the previous mudrā, perform the mudrā.
The mantra is as follows:

Oṃ bhubhu jvāle tṛkā tṛtathāgata-āyācaye. [Perform the mudrās for] the invitation, the hook, the noose, the chain, and the bell; then, for the luster of all offering substances, use the three-pronged mudrā.
The mantra is:
Oṃ jvalāya mantre svāhā. Next, sprinkle purified water with bamboo leaves.
Then recite the Amṛta-mantra as follows:
Extend the right hand over the right shoulder, keeping the fingers together and the middle finger extended.
Recite this twenty-one times:
*Namo surope tathāgata tadyathā oṃ suru surupa ra surupa ra suru svāhā*. Next, recite the heart mantra of Vairocana.
Recite the Mantra for Turning the Ocean of Milk.
Extend the five fingers of the right hand downward;
as you bring it over the vessel of food, it is immediately transformed.
Visualize the syllable *vaṃ* within the palm of the hand.
Then recite the mantra: *Namo samantabuddhānāṃ vaṃ*.
This causes the offering substances to become of exquisite flavor.
Next, one may invite the Lord of Mount Tai;
this is the king’s residence.
Behind the mountain resides the valiant King of Ghosts.
In an instant, one travels through the worlds.
Regarding the "plank-disease" (*kāṣṭhaka*), this is a synonym for pestilence (*mārī*).
With the vajra-palms joined, one may recite the mantra.
*Namo samantabuddhānāṃ citrāpātāya svāhā.* Next, one may request offerings for the various classes of spirits.
Next, recite the names of the five Tathāgatas from the heart:
*Namo bhagavate prabhūtaratnāya tathāgatāya*. Homage to the Tathāgata Prabhūtaratna, who eliminates the karma of stinginess and greed and whose merit and virtue are perfectly complete.
Namo bhagavate surūpāya tathāgatāya. Homage to the Tathāgata of Wondrous Form, who destroys ugly appearances and is perfected with the marks and signs of excellence.
Namo bhagavate amṛtāya rājñe | Tathāgatāya namo amṛtarājāya tathāgatāya. This is the empowerment of the Dharma for the body and mind; may it cause them to receive happiness.
Namo bhagavate vipulagātrāya tathāgatāya. Namo to the Tathāgata of Vast Body, whose throat is wide and who partakes of exquisite flavors.
Namo bhagavate aparājitakārāya tathāgatāya | Namo to the Tathāgata Aparājita, who removes all fear and completely eliminates the realm of hungry ghosts.
Next, with vajra-anjali, one should respectfully invoke Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva,
praying that through his compassion he may cause all those in the realms of the dead to proceed in due order and not lose their proper place.
Next, one may recite while maintaining vajra-anjali.
We, [Name] and others, respectfully offer these fragrant and pure foods, as well as money, coins, silks, and other such items, first to the Buddhas of the ten directions—

equal in number to the atoms within hundreds of thousands of koṭis, millions of nayutas, and unspeakably unspeakable numbers of lands— to all the spirits of the hidden officials and hidden paths, the monks and nuns, the numinous realms, the five hundred classes of hungry ghosts, the celestial Brahmins, and the various hosts of hungry ghosts.
Each individual obtains sixteen *shu* of food from the kingdom of Magadha,
which they are able to transform entirely into a pure ocean of milk— the nectar and clarified butter of the joy of Dharma and the delight of dhyāna.
Pervading the entire dharma realm,
vast and immeasurable, there is none that is not fully satisfied;
all have universally realized liberation and bodhi.
I take refuge in the eternally abiding Triple Gem.
Next, with vajra palms joined,
recite the praise as follows:

Ārya-avalokiteśvara-sura-kinnara-nara-kinnara-jātya-pravaradharma-garbhodgata-vi-dharma-cāpraśama-cakṣya-nimitta-buddha-nimitta-parākāśaya-tan-ha-śrīmānaya-dhama. Then, chant the verse of confession: "Today, whatever offerings I have prepared..."
It is largely contrary to the Dharma;
it is laughable, coarse, and evil,
causing distress and confusion to all the officials of the underworld, the paths of the dead, and the assembly of *dānagil* spirits.
O beings of the dark realms, we only pray that you grant us permission; we only pray that you will compassionately bestow upon us joy and happiness.
Next, if one wishes to eliminate pestilence, wind-related illnesses, or malaria:
One may offer [this] to the Great Mountain Lord (Mahāparvateśvara).
Furthermore, if one wishes to be liberated from the curses of wicked people and enemies,
one may separately offer it to the positions of Mahābrahmā and the Four Heavenly Kings (Cāturmahārājika), and one will immediately attain liberation.

If one wishes to obtain merit and fortune, one may separately make offerings to the twenty-eight great yakṣas who are the retinue of Vaiśravaṇa. If one wishes to rescue and deliver the life of the primary karmic retribution, [one should do so].
One may separately make offerings to King Yama and the Generals of the Five Paths;
thus, one shall immediately have one’s name removed from the register of the dead and inscribed upon the register of the living.
All matters depend entirely upon the practitioner’s intention.
However, there is no need to offer money, coins, silk, or the like.
When the ācārya summons the specific nāgas, spirits, and all other deities, they may be offered upon a separate seat according to one's inclination.
Always take a new garment, pierce a hole in its center, and place it within the mandala.
At every session, exit the mandala while reciting the mantra of King Yama,
and offer fried cakes and porridge made of the five grains.
Add various fragrant flowers and water to the purification vessel,
and with a joyful mind, scatter them in the four directions,
beginning with the four spirits.
All the spirits and others shall joyfully accept [this offering],
after which one may read the Mahāyāna sūtras.
*The Sequential Offering to Yama*, Volume One.
